We assume that a solution of our equation has the following Fourier series:

$$
{y}_{p}∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi x).
$$

Now, we compute the derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p}^{′} & ∼\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi x))∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}n\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi x) \\ {y}_{p}^{″} & ∼\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}n\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi x))∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }-{b}_{n}{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi x)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the expressions for ${y}_{p}^{″}$ and ${y}_{p}$ into the equation and have

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }-{b}_{n}{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi x)-8(\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi x))=8+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{3(-1)^{n+1}}{{n}^{3}\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi x).
$$

Rearranging the terms, we get 

$$
-8\cdot \frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}(-{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}-8)\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi x)=8+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{3(-1)^{n+1}}{{n}^{3}\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi x).
$$

Now, equating the free terms and sine coefficients, we obtain:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-8\cdot \frac{{a}_{0}}{2}=8 \\ {b}_{n}(-{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}-8)=\frac{3(-1)^{n+1}}{{n}^{3}\pi }\end{aligned}\,⇒\,{\begin{aligned}\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}=-1 \\ {b}_{n}=\frac{3(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{3}\pi ({n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}+8)}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
{y}_{p}∼-1+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,\frac{3(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{3}\pi ({n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}+8)}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi x).
$$
